issue_plan.name: Reader statecharts for modeled proposals
issue_plan.summary: These ten issues make every modeled proposal explain its behavior with a reader's statechart computed from TLC, so people can see what they are being asked to ratify. They add charts for fork options, comparisons for revisions and amendments, numbered known-bug paths, and an explicit smaller-bound or paths-only view for large models, in that order. Invariant then renders the same charts as SVG for receipts and the dashboard, while Markdown receipts retain the Mermaid text. Plumbing proposals get no chart, and every issue updates the current-state documentation.

issues.title: Expose complete TLC graphs for reader statecharts
issues.body:
Issue #571 requires the factory to compute reader statecharts from TLC's actual reachable states and action-labeled steps. Add a reusable, lossless graph result under internal/tlc, using the pinned TLC and its -dump dot,actionlabels output. internal/tlc/graph.go already runs that dump; internal/dashboard/graph.go parses it into a dashboard-specific form and later samples edges. The new result must be available outside the dashboard before any display compaction.

Retain concrete state identities, exact variable values, every initial state, and each dumped source/action/target step, including self-loops and parallel actions. Return TLC's completed-run statistics and the graph's state and step counts with the bounds and tool provenance. Distinguish generated-state statistics from the number of graph steps. Preserve the existing Dump caller contract or adapt its callers compatibly; do not reuse the dashboard's sampled graph as complete evidence.

A malformed, incomplete, failed or canceled dump must not become a successful graph. Reuse the runner's admission, resource limits and cancellation cleanup, with isolated outputs so an earlier run cannot supply a graph. This change supplies graph data only; proposal rendering comes in a later issue.

Acceptance covers pinned-TLC dump fixtures and a real-tool integration case, multiple initial states, loops, distinct action labels on the same endpoints, exact structured values, invalid or truncated input, cancellation and stale output refusal. Existing dashboard graph behavior remains covered.

Update SPEC.md, a short README description linking docs/statecharts.md, and that new page to describe the graph foundation actually delivered. Follow AGENTS.md's decision-recording and documentation rules.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Compute faithful reader statecharts from pure views
issues.body:
Build the reader-statechart computation in internal/statechart on the complete TLC graph API delivered earlier in #571's plan. The drafting agent supplies only a view: state(vars) names a concrete state in the reader's words, and step(action, from, to) names a concrete transition or requests that it be hidden. Define a serializable view format and a constrained evaluator that enforces deterministic, side-effect-free evaluation without I/O, imports, process execution or mutable state. Evaluation errors and missing mappings are refusals, not dropped states.

Every reachable concrete state must map to exactly one chart state, and every chart arrow must come from concrete TLC steps. Preserve initial-state membership and the concrete members of each chart state and arrow. Use TLC-evaluated invariant results to prevent merging states that violate different rules; temporal violations are facts about traces, not predicates to invent for individual states.

Validate hiding against the full graph: every chart state stays reachable from a chart initial state; every chart state with an outgoing step before hiding keeps an outgoing arrow; and the concrete steps belonging to one chart arrow are either all shown or all hidden. Refuse violations with the offending states, actions and hiding rule so the drafting agent can fix its view. Aim for about 20 arrows through the view, without making that a hard cap or dropping evidence to meet it.

Produce deterministic chart data and a report. For each chart state, list the model actions that none of its concrete members takes although some other reachable state does, computed before hiding. Include the lock's exact says words for the rules, all hidden steps with their labels and counts, and both TLC and chart state/step counts with their meanings. Support the full input through 500 reachable TLC states; report larger input explicitly until the later large-model issue supplies its fallback.

Acceptance covers a small lifecycle projection, every hiding refusal, mixed enabled/disabled actions within a chart state, rule-distinct states, total mapping, deterministic replay, evaluator isolation and faithful counts. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description and docs/statecharts.md for this computation and its current size limit.

issues.title: Show the reader statechart in every modeled proposal
issues.body:
Connect #571's checked reader-statechart computation to modeled drafting and proposal comments. Today internal/formalize reads a module and proposal.json, runs verify.RunModel, and internal/factory/comments.go publishes statements without a reader chart. Extend the drafting prompt and workspace contract so the agent writes its pure view beside the model. The check tool and the factory's independent final check must compute the chart from that exact model at the proposal's bounds. The agent never supplies chart topology or final Mermaid as evidence.

Publish a factory-generated Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 in new modeled proposal, revision and amendment comments. Beside it show the per-state actions that cannot happen, the rules in the lock's exact says words, the hidden steps, TLC's state and step counts, the chart's counts and the checked bounds. Escape labels and rule text so they remain literal content. Keep the existing statement tables, checks and ratification instructions. Missing or invalid views and dishonest hiding return actionable check feedback and prevent publication as a usable modeled proposal. Above the current 500-state capacity, report the size limitation explicitly; the later large-model step replaces that limitation with a labeled fallback.

Carry the view and computed snapshot through formalization.json, persisted proposals, recovered runs, previous-draft staging and the project written at ratification. Bind derived artifacts to the exact model, includes, view, bounds and pinned tools so changed inputs cannot reuse stale charts. This explanation must preserve existing statement hashes, lock semantics and proof claims; it is not a new ratified invariant. Keep older stored proposals readable and leave plumbing and plans of issues chart-free.

Acceptance exercises draft check feedback and repair, the independent final check, posting and recovery, saved view round trips, changed-input invalidation, literal rendering and the absence of charts on plumbing proposals. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description, docs/statecharts.md and the relevant drafting description in docs/factory.md.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Draw a checked statechart for each modeled fork option
issues.body:
Extend modeled decision requests so each fork option carries its own reader statechart before anyone chooses it. This builds on the saved views, checked chart data and Mermaid rendering already delivered for #571. internal/formalize currently permits forks without a module, and its prompt explicitly says not to draft one; change that modeled-fork contract to accept an isolated preview model, bounds, candidate rules and view for every option.

Check each preview with pinned TLC and the same chart and hiding validation as a modeled proposal. Associate all inputs, diagnostics and chart output with the exact fork and option IDs, and retain them through saved results and factory recovery. A missing, invalid or mismatched preview must be returned to the drafting agent to repair rather than published as a checked option. Each option chart uses its own candidate rules' says words, counts, hidden-step report and named bounds.

Render the option's words and its stateDiagram-v2 together in internal/factory/comments.go so a reader can compare the behaviors in one decision request. Previews respect choices already made and cannot silently decide other unanswered forks. They are alternatives awaiting a person's choice: previewing an option neither ratifies its rules nor starts a build. Existing partial-answer and revision behavior stays intact, and plumbing or PRD-planning forks still have no model chart.

Acceptance covers two options with observably different transitions, multiple forks, partial answers and restart, option-ID mixups, invalid views, independent preview failures and chart-free plumbing forks. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description, docs/statecharts.md and docs/factory.md to describe option previews.

issues.title: Show chart states and arrows changed by revisions and amendments
issues.body:
Add a reader-statechart comparison to modeled proposal comments. For a revision of a new project, compare with the immediately preceding proposal snapshot. For an amendment, compare with the existing project's ratified model and lock captured as the amendment's baseline. Name the baseline proposal or ratification and its model/view identity beside the comparison, so readers know what changed against what.

Use the snapshots retained by the earlier #571 issues and extend internal/formalize/diff.go, Current/Target staging and internal/factory/comments.go. Show the chart states and labeled arrows added and removed, retaining the complete new chart and the existing statement/bound diff. Compare canonical chart identities and endpoints, independent of DOT ordering or layout. A changed reader label or hiding choice must be visible and identified as a view change; it must not silently erase a behavioral difference. Show both bounds when they differ and identify differences caused by the displayed scope.

When the baseline predates saved views, have the drafting agent supply a baseline view over an immutable copy of the old model and lock, and validate it with the same TLC-backed machinery. It cannot edit old statements, model bytes or bounds to make the comparison fit. Never substitute the latest branch contents for the captured baseline, or treat a missing comparison as an empty graph. Make baseline failures actionable during drafting.

Acceptance covers added and removed states and arrows, unchanged graphs in different dump order, label and hiding changes, bound changes, legacy baselines, consecutive revisions, amendment baselines and restart from saved results. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description, docs/statecharts.md and docs/factory.md to explain exactly what each comparison means.

issues.title: Draw each known bug as a numbered TLC path
issues.body:
Show each modeled proposal's known-bug check as a numbered path through the reader's state names, ending at the rule the bug breaks. Use the real counterexample produced by the existing check that adds that bug to Next, never an agent-authored path or a shortest route recomputed on the collapsed chart. internal/verify currently writes bug trace files only when outDir is set, while RunModel uses no output directory; retain trace data for model-only drafting as well as ordinary verification without changing whether a bug is caught.

For invariant bugs, use TLC's breadth-first counterexample, the shortest path it finds within the stated bounds. Keep the concrete step order and numbering even when consecutive states share a reader label. Label the planted action and the violated rule with the lock's says words. Map the violating state too, keeping different violated-rule sets distinct, and never hide the violating step. Link the path to its bug/check identity, source snapshot and bounds.

Known bugs may also expect temporal properties. Preserve tlc.TraceFile's loop target or stuttering ending and label these as TLC's looping counterexamples; do not turn them into finite safety failures or claim a shortest finite path that TLC did not establish. A failed, uncaught or missing-trace check displays its actual diagnostic, never a fabricated successful bug path.

Render these paths with the proposal's existing Mermaid/chart report and retain their structured data for later SVG and receipts. Acceptance covers a shortest safety trace with a longer alternative, repeated reader states, a violation outside the correct graph, multiple bugs, property loops and stuttering, failed checks and model-only trace retention. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description, docs/statecharts.md and the known-bug description in docs/gate.md.

issues.title: Explain models above 500 states with smaller charts or paths
issues.body:
Complete #571's large-model behavior across modeled proposals, fork previews, comparisons and known-bug displays. The full reader chart is available through 500 reachable TLC states at the proposal's bounds. Above that threshold, support an explicitly supplied smaller display bound and otherwise fall back to checked paths only. A smaller-bound chart must come from its own completed pinned-TLC exploration with no more than 500 reachable states and must pass the same view and hiding checks.

Keep proposal and ratified checking bounds intact. Show the original bounds and full-check counts separately from the display bounds and display-run counts, with an explicit 'smaller-bound chart' or 'paths only' label. If a smaller display bound is absent, invalid, still too large or cannot yield a complete graph, use real reachability and known-bug paths from the checks, naming their bounds and coverage. Retain witness traces where needed for this positive-behavior view. Do not substitute a sampled or truncated DOT graph for a complete chart, and do not infer globally impossible actions from the absence of an action in selected paths. Unknown full counts stay unavailable.

View-invalidity remains a refusal to fix, not a reason to silently bypass the honesty checks. Preserve failed-check diagnostics and never lower verification bounds to obtain a passing chart. Comparisons explicitly identify their display modes and scopes; a change of scope or unavailable full graph cannot masquerade as behavior added or removed. Keep chart work bounded and cancellable without relaxing the verifier's resource policies.

Acceptance covers exactly 500 and 501 states, a successful smaller-bound display, no smaller bound, invalid or still-large bounds, paths with no complete graph, separate verification/display counts, changing comparison scopes and cancellation without stale fallback artifacts. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description and docs/statecharts.md to describe both large-model modes and their limits.

issues.title: Render reader statecharts as SVG inside Invariant
issues.body:
Add a native SVG renderer to internal/statechart for the checked chart and path data delivered by #571. It must render ordinary statecharts, fork-option charts, added/removed state and arrow annotations, numbered bug paths and the labeled large-model display modes. Invariant computes the layout and writes the SVG itself; no Mermaid, Graphviz or other rendering script is loaded or executed when a person views the result.

Render initial states, directed labeled arrows, self-loops, distinct parallel arrows, multiline reader labels and path step numbers legibly. Preserve all chart data and display qualifications rather than hiding edges to simplify layout. Include accessible titles/descriptions and a usable viewBox. Stable input yields stable SVG. Treat all model and reader text as literal XML text, with no scripts, event handlers, foreignObject content or external resource references introduced by labels.

Expose one renderer that the subsequent receipt and dashboard issues can share, alongside the existing Mermaid serializer; both must represent the same checked states, arrows and paths. This change delivers the standalone renderer, without requiring dashboard or receipt integration to be part of this pull request.

Acceptance covers loops and parallel edges, long and special-character labels, disconnected path panels, added/removed styling, temporal loops, deterministic output and SVG inspection for active content or external dependencies. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description and docs/statecharts.md to describe the native renderer actually available.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Include reader statecharts in verification receipts
issues.body:
Carry #571's reader charts into the receipts emitted for modeled projects, using the native SVG renderer already delivered. Extend the verification/report and receipt paths in internal/verify, internal/receipt and cmd/invariant, including synthesis and factory-produced gate receipts. Recompute the chart from the exact model being verified and the saved project view; synthesis can change the draft model, so a proposal chart alone is not evidence of the built model's behavior. Ensure project staging retains the view needed for this computation.

Retain structured chart data and source provenance with the receipt, write standalone SVG artifacts with output receipts, and include the Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 text in Markdown receipts. Carry the rules' says words, impossible-action report where full exploration supports it, hidden steps, counts, bounds, bug paths and large-model mode. Reuse the common chart pipeline and serializers so the formats agree. Receipt output remains usable offline and needs no viewer-side rendering script for its SVG.

Keep chart presentation and chart-generation diagnostics separate from verification assurance: a chart is an explanation, not additional proof, and its presence cannot change a failed check into a pass. Old reports and modeled projects without a saved view remain readable and explicitly lack a reader chart until a view is supplied; never invent one from raw TLA+ labels. Plumbing receipts have no chart. Existing locks and evidence retain their compatibility.

Acceptance exercises CLI output files, receipt JSON round trips, factory/synthesis receipts, changed model/view invalidation, full and paths-only charts, known-bug paths, generation failures, legacy reports and chart-free plumbing. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description, docs/statecharts.md and docs/gate.md for the delivered receipt formats.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Show reader statecharts on the dashboard without a rendering script
issues.body:
Integrate #571's checked reader charts and Invariant-generated SVG into the dashboard. internal/dashboard currently reads CI receipt archives, dumps project graphs itself and sends compacted graph JSON to browser drawing code. Add the reader-statechart presentation using the structured receipt artifacts and shared native renderer already delivered, bound to the exact receipt/model/view snapshot. Do not rebuild a reader chart from the existing sampled Graph.Compact output.

Serve the SVG from Invariant with appropriate content type and cache identity, and display it on the modeled project's evidence view with its rules, impossible actions where supported, hidden steps, state/step counts, bug paths and named bounds or paths-only qualification. Make the chart available as a standalone SVG that renders with JavaScript disabled and without loading a chart-rendering library at page view. Existing dashboard scripts may still fetch status and insert an image; they must not compute the chart or be required to render the SVG itself.

Include chart format, model/view/bounds/tool provenance and displayed report content in invalidation so a refreshed or restarted dashboard cannot serve an old explanation for new evidence. Keep repository/project identities separate, preserve the current public/private access boundaries, and show a clear unavailable state for old receipts without a reader view or failed chart generation. Retain the existing raw graph view as separate detail where useful, with its own coverage labels; plumbing cards remain chart-free.

Acceptance covers receipt archive loading, SVG HTTP responses, a script-disabled standalone view, full and large-model modes, known-bug paths, label escaping, cache changes and restart, multiple repositories, legacy receipts and plumbing cards. Update SPEC.md, the README's short linked description, docs/statecharts.md and docs/dashboard.md to state the completed behavior.
